Applying to the Graduate Program
Applications for graduate study in the School of Mathematical and Statistical Sciences are submitted through the Clemson University Graduate School. Applications submitted electronically are most efficiently processed and are highly recommended. The department does have some requirements, however, as to what is included as part of your application.
Application Details
Requirements
Students apply to the graduate program in the school will be required to submit official transcripts from your undergraduate and graduate institutions. Read the Clemson University Graduate School policy on transcripts.
TEST SCORES: Be sure that your official test scores are sent directly from the Educational Testing Service to Clemson. Clemson University’s school code is 5111. The School of Mathematical and Statistical Sciences requires international students to submit TOEFL scores and recommends that all students submit GRE general test scores. Note: The GRE general test scores are not required.
RECOMMENDATIONS: Three letters of recommendation are required. You will be asked to submit the names and email addresses of your recommenders on the online application. Your recommenders will receive instructions on submitting their recommendations from the application system.
STATEMENT: A one-page statement of your academic interests can improve your chances for admission. This statement should include your area of interest, career plans and an indication of why you selected Clemson University.
All application materials must be submitted through the online application system or sent directly to the Office of Graduate Admissions.
Fees
The application fee will no longer be charged for anyone applying to Summer 2023 and beyond. Learn more about application and admission process on the Graduate School website.
Deadlines
If you are applying for admission in the fall term (which begins in mid-August), it is recommended that you submit your application materials by Jan. 15. If you are applying for the spring term (which begins in early January), submit application materials by Oct. 1. Completed applications received after these dates may still be considered for admission and financial aid. International applicants should check with the International Services for additional deadlines.
Acceptance and Financial Support
The most important criterion for admission is whether a student’s background and ability are sufficient to indicate successful completion of the degree program. Selection for financial aid is more competitive than just admission to the school. Additionally, the goal of our assistantship program is the development of excellent teachers. International students will be required to pass the Verification of English Skills Test in order to maintain any assistantship offered.
Find out more about financial aid options for graduate students.
Explore additional information regarding the VEST.
